pages.text: Grandma washed rice in the kitchen. Swish, swish. Dingding stood on tiptoe to see.
"Today I will measure the water." Dingding stood a finger on the rice. "Yesterday, it reached here."
Grandma dipped her big hand in. "Perfect when it covers the back of my hand."
Water poured up to the back of her hand.
Dingding tried a finger. Water reached three joints! "Yesterday, only one."
"My hand was always right." Grandma closed the lid.
Rice ready! Lid off, a puff of steam. The grains were soggy.
Dingding held a hand beside Grandma's. Hers was much bigger and thicker. "Our hands are different!"
Next day, Dingding poured water and stopped at one finger joint.
Each rice grain gleamed. Grandma looked at her hand. "Next time, I must borrow your finger."
